<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

</asp>

<asp>

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.

#show output/3.
</asp>

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Determine grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Each cell that must receive exactly one colour
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Zero cells stay zero
output(R,C,0) :- input(R,C,0).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Helper: all rows between the original position R and the
% target position Rout (Rout ≥ R) are empty (contain a zero)
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout = R, true.
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout > R,
    input(Rout, C, 0),
    empty_between(C,R,Rout-1).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% A non‑zero cell can fall (gravity) to a row Rout (≥ R)
% It stops either at the bottom of the grid or just below a
% non‑zero cell.
can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),           % original cell (must be non‑zero)
    V != 0,                 % we only move non‑zero cells
    Rout >= R,              % move downwards (increase row index)
    empty_between(C,R,Rout),% rows between must be empty
    Rout = N-1, n_rows(N).  % bottom of the grid (first stopping case)

can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),
    V != 0,
    Rout >= R,
    empty_between(C,R,Rout),
    not input(Rout+1, C, _).% second stopping case (blocked by a non‑zero below)

output(Rout, C, V) :- can_fall(R,C,V,Rout).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R, C, Col) : Col : colour(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

#show output/3.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  ARC – “Gravity” style transformation
%  Each colour slides downwards in its column until it would hit
%  another non‑zero cell (or the bottom of the grid).  The relative
%  order of colours inside a column is preserved – blocks move together.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- row(N).
col(0..M-1) :- col(M).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one colour for each output cell
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
1 { output(R,C,Col) : Col : colour(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Helper predicate: cells in a column that are zero
% empty_between(C,Rout,R)  is true iff every row between R and
% Rout (exclusive of R, inclusive of Rout) is zero.
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout >= R, Rout = R, true.
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout > R,
                      input(Rout,C,0),
                      empty_between(C,R,Rout-1).

% A cell (R,C,V) can fall to row Rout (Rout >= R) iff
% the rows between R and Rout are all zero and the cell just
% below Rout is either the bottom of the grid or a non‑zero cell.
can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),
    Rout >= R,
    empty_between(C,R,Rout),
    (Rout = n_rows-1 ; not input(Rout+1,C,_)).

% Apply the fall – each original cell ends up at its final position
output(Rout,C,V) :- can_fall(R,C,V,Rout).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Show the result
#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Empty rows between cell at R and target Rout (moving upwards)
empty_up(C,R,Rout) :- Rout = R, true.
empty_up(C,R,Rout) :- Rout < R,
    input(Rout, C, 0),
    empty_up(C,R,Rout+1).

% A cell can move up to Rout (<=R) if the rows between are empty and
% it stops either at the top row or just below a non-zero cell.
can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),
    Rout <= R,
    empty_up(C,R,Rout),
    (Rout = 0) ;
    (Rout > 0, input(Rout-1, C, _)).

output(Rout, C, V) :- can_fall(R,C,V,Rout).

% Exactly one output colour per output cell
1 { output(R, C, Col) : Col : colour(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Helper: all rows between the original position R and the
% target position Rout (Rout ≥ R) are empty (contain a zero)
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout = R, true.
empty_between(C,R,Rout) :- Rout > R,
    input(Rout, C, 0),
    empty_between(C,R,Rout-1).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% A non‑zero cell can fall (gravity) to a row Rout (≥ R)
% It stops either at the bottom of the grid or just below a
% non‑zero cell.
can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),           % original cell (must be non‑zero)
    V != 0,                 % we only move non‑zero cells
    Rout >= R,              % move downwards (increase row index)
    empty_between(C,R,Rout),% rows between must be empty
    Rout = N-1, n_rows(N).  % bottom of the grid (first stopping case)

can_fall(R,C,V,Rout) :-
    input(R,C,V),
    V != 0,
    Rout >= R,
    empty_between(C,R,Rout),
    not input(Rout+1, C, _).% second stopping case (blocked by a non‑zero below)

output(Rout, C, V) :- can_fall(R,C,V,Rout).

% -------------------------------------------------------------
% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R, C, Col) : Col : colour(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).
